basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; pectus excavatum 7/11, strabismus 5/11 and hearing impairment 5/11 support additional axes.
Structural hair-shaft dysplasia; hair belongs to the dermatologic axis.
Anterior segment dysgenesis; hearing impairment and cardiovascular malformations each 30-79%; dental and pituitary abnormalities reported below 30%.
Benign tumour arising in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary tract damage is not established.
Immune dysregulation; bronchiectasis 7/10, splenic lymphoproliferation 6/6 and ileitis 2/2; cap excludes smaller-series skin, joint and vascular findings.
Amenorrhea-galactorrhea is a prolactin-related endocrine syndrome; reproductive and breast manifestations do not supply additional axes.
Parkinsonism and motor-sensory polyneuropathy affect the central and peripheral nervous systems.
Immune-mediated neuroinflammatory movement disorder; opsoclonus reflects neurologic dysfunction, and associated tumours are separate diseases.
Focal or multifocal dystonia is neurologic; laryngeal and lingual dystonia do not establish intrinsic airway or gastrointestinal damage.
Neoplasm arising in the ethmoid sinus, within the airway axis; lymphoma is only one possible histologic subtype.
Idiopathic osteolysis and osteonecrosis of the phalangeal bones.
Motor-sensory neuropathy classified as a glycolysis disorder; persistent foot deformities include pes cavus in 19/21 patients.
Primary skeletal dysplasia affecting humeri, hips, digits and vertebrae; facial appearance does not establish other organ damage.
Carcinoma originates in the thyroid endocrine gland; other reported cancers are separate diseases and each occurs in 1/4 patients.
Umbrella disorder of the vermiform appendix; infection or immune mechanisms do not apply across all subtypes.
CoQ10 deficiency with encephalopathy and cardiomyopathy; hearing impairment 10/14; muscle involvement omitted at cap; respiratory failure may be neuromuscular.
Vascular and skeletal connective-tissue disorder; abnormal skin scarring and oral clefts each 30-79%; asthma is separate and blue sclerae do not impair vision.
Occlusive retinal capillary disease causes progressive visual loss; associated systemic or cerebral occlusive diseases are separate conditions.
CNS hypomyelination with regression and spastic tetraplegia; scoliosis in one reported patient does not establish common direct skeletal involvement.
Hydrocephalus, joint laxity and kyphosis define the syndrome; aortic regurgitation is reported as frequent, 30-79%.
Benign proliferation of cutaneous lymphatic endothelial channels, typically forming persistent skin plaques; not lymphoma.
Tuberculosis directly affects lung and pleura, with cavitary rupture producing pneumothorax.
Defined mitochondrial complex IV deficiency with infantile encephalocardiomyopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 2/2; separate skeletal myopathy not established.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with speech and motor delay; no defined systemic metabolic defect or additional organ damage is supplied.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia with motor axonal neuropathy and intellectual disability; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic ocular damage.
